summary: boxy-constants ships a load-time remote binary dropper with obfuscated C2
details: On require of the package, index.js loads _shim.js which reconstructs attacker-controlled hostnames from split-string arrays (Cloudflare Workers subdomains such as oob-worker.cf100-41.6.workers.dev and *.dl.wel1.ru), selects an OS/arch-specific URL for linux_x64/linux_arm64/darwin/win32, fetches an unsigned, unhashed binary via https.get, writes it to /var/tmp/.cache_<hex> on POSIX or %TEMP%\dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe on Windows, chmods 0755, and detaches it via spawn("/bin/sh",["-c", fp+" &"]) or cmd /c start. A DNS-TXT base64 channel provides a fallback host-resolution path. A marker file '.analytics_state' implements cooldown-based execution suppression, and a stealth logger writes empty strings to stderr. Decoy filenames (dotnet_diag_,.cache_) and 'analytics/telemetry' naming disguise the dropper. require("child_"+"process") is used to hide the sensitive API from static scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
